title: Day 52 · Week 7, Day 3 — Parents: when to tell people — the twelve-week rule against the evidence, the one woman in nine who has been there, the workplace numbers, and the first shot of the pregnancy, which is also yours
summary: The fourth Parents episode. Your baby is 9–11 mm at Carnegie stage 16: dark eyes, a wrist, finger rays three days away. The twelve-week rule, taken apart: it is arithmetically right about the loss curve (a quarter of hormone-detected conceptions gone before 6 weeks, Wilcox 1999; 10% at age 25–29, Magnus 2019; ~4% after a heartbeat at 7 weeks, Tong 2008) and socially backwards about what people are for. What people believe (Bardos 2015, n = 1,084): 55% think miscarriage happens in ≤5% of pregnancies, 76% blame stress, 64% lifting; of those who had one, 47% felt guilty, 41% alone, 28% ashamed, and 28% felt less isolated when a public figure spoke. What is true (Quenby, Lancet 2021): 15.3% of recognised pregnancies, 23 million a year, and 10.8% of women have had one — one in nine. What a loss does (Farren 2020, 737 women): PTSD criteria in 29% at one month and 18% at nine, anxiety 24% → 17%, depression 11% → 6%; partners (Farren 2021, 192 couples): 7%, 6% and 2% at one month, 4%, 6% and 1% at nine. What support does: low support and antenatal depression AOR 1.18 and anxiety 1.97 after correcting publication bias (Bedaso 2021, 64,449 women); miscarriage and low support compounding rather than adding for later depression in 179,000 UK Biobank women (Hu 2024); support programmes not changing birth weight or preterm birth (Cochrane 2019, 25 trials). The early list and the scan list, and whose decision it is. Work: 77% of UK mothers with a negative or discriminatory experience and 11% dismissed, made redundant or forced out (~54,000 a year); the US Pregnant Workers Fairness Act (June 2023, 15+ employees, accommodations once the limitation is communicated, no note for common needs, no retaliation); UK notice at 15 weeks before the expected week of childbirth, with protections starting when the employer knows. Then the flu shot: 5% of 2009 pandemic deaths from the ~1% of the population that was pregnant, 22.6% of hospitalised women to ICU, treatment after day 4 carrying 6× the ICU risk (Siston 2010); nearly half of hospitalised women aged 15–49 pregnant in autumn 2022 (CDC); 40% protection against flu hospitalisation across 2 million pregnancies (Thompson 2019); 63% fewer confirmed infant infections in Bangladesh (Zaman 2008, 340 mothers) and 50.4%/48.8% maternal/infant efficacy in South Africa (Madhi 2014, 2,116 women); the miscarriage signal (Donahue 2017, aOR 2.0, 7.7 in repeat vaccinees) and the prospective null that followed (Donahue 2019, aOR 0.9, 1,236 cases); Cochrane's healthy-adult numbers for the father (2.3% → 0.9%, NNV 71); ACIP 2025–26 (inactivated, any trimester, September–October preferred for the first and second trimester, single-dose thimerosal-free, no nasal spray) and the NHS (all pregnant women, any stage, from September).
action: Fifteen minutes tonight, one sheet, two columns. Left: the people you would both want to already know if it went wrong — the ones who would just show up; she decides every name and you say which of them are yours. Right: everyone else, with the scan date from the Day 42 card as the default. The first row of the left column gets told this week, in her words. Underneath: her flu shot booked for this week if the season is open where you live (inactivated, not the spray), and yours booked for the same day at the same pharmacy; if the season isn't open yet, the month it opens goes in your calendar now.
